thread:
anya_pm: Quick heads up — Sales flagged a competitor push (they shipped a 'SmartCache' style feature). Multiple customers are asking for similar parity. We need to decide whether to prioritize 'shared prefix/KV caching' or keep focusing on 'adaptive quantization' for Q2. Can we do a quick triage here?

sam-l: Short answer: prefix KV MVP is smaller, higher immediate impact for chat-heavy customers. Rough estimate: 3 sprints for a minimal end-to-end path (cache + eviction + metrics).

jordan-eng: Adding context — quantization work reduces cost across all workloads but needs model validation + CI/eval time. That's more like 2–3 months with current infra backlog.

maria_cs: From CS: at least 3 enterprise customers said they'd expand Dedicated commitments if we ship prefix sharing. One called it a "deal accelerator".

li_sales: +1 from AE side. We're seeing RFPs that explicitly compare our caching behavior to CompetitorX. If we don't show something soon we risk losing momentum.

anya_pm: Proposed rubric to decide: 1) near-term revenue uplift 2) engineering effort (sprints) 3) competitive parity risk 4) long-term differentiation. Quick matrix idea below. Thoughts?

sam-l: Matrix looks fine. Quick notes: effort numbers are rough — need eng triage to confirm. Also need to know maintenance ops cost (SLO impact).

jordan-eng: Also consider rollout complexity: prefix KV needs fallback and canary to avoid stale responses. We'll want per-customer toggle + metrics (cache hit rate, latency p95). That adds ~1 sprint of infra work.

anya_pm: Putting a sketch here (pasted from my notes):

```
Feature                    | Revenue | Effort (sprints) | Parity risk | Diff impact
---------------------------|---------|------------------|-------------|------------
Shared prefix / KV caching | High    | 3                | High        | Medium     
Adaptive quantization      | Med     | 8                | Low         | High       
```

li_sales: If we weight revenue higher (we're in pipeline push), KV wins. If we weight differentiation higher, quantization eventually wins.

maria_cs: Customer asks also include "explainable cache behavior" — audit logs, TTL controls. That could be scoped as MVP-1 vs MVP-2.

sam-l: Suggestion: split workstreams. Fast path = prefix KV basic (MVP: per-model prefix cache, TTL, per-customer toggle). Parallel long path = start exploratory quantization spikes + eval harness. That buys us both lanes.

anya_pm: OK I like split stream. Proposed launch criteria for KV MVP: 1) end-to-end correctness on chat traces 2) cache hit rate >= 10% on pilot tenants 3) SLO: p95 latency not increased >5% 4) feature flag and per-tenant opt-in.

jordan-eng: For the quantization spike, define success metrics: latency reduction >20% for embedding/generation, no degradation on quality evals (eval delta <= 1% on our benchmark).

li_sales: Actionable ask: can we commit to a Beta for KV within 6 weeks? Customers want a pilot timeline.

sam-l: 6 weeks is tight but possible if we cut scope: no cross-model dedupe, no fancy eviction policy, just simple LRU + TTL + per-tenant toggle. Ops will need a canary path.

anya_pm: I'll capture scope as: KV Beta (6 weeks): LRU + TTL, per-tenant toggle, basic telemetry. Engineering to confirm sprint plan by EOD tomorrow.

maria_cs: I'll line up two pilot customers and draft pilot plan + success criteria (CS metrics + billing experiment).

li_sales: I'll update the opportunities and let AEs know pilot window.

release-bot: Note: scheduled infra maintenance next Tuesday 02:00–04:00 UTC. If engineering needs early canary, ping infra squad.

anya_pm: Cool — next steps: sam-l to confirm scope/plan by EOD, jordan to spin up quantization spike backlog items, maria to prep pilots, li to update sales comms. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
